Subject: Hosted→Dedicated migration exploration + stress test windows

Hi Sofia,

Thanks for the quick demo last week — the team liked the throughput and the latency consistency. We're starting to lock down the migration plan off hosted into a dedicated pool and want Redwood's sizing validation and a realistic cutover cadence. High-level context below: 

- Production profile: mostly short chat sessions with occasional long-form summarization. Typical concurrent user sessions: 1,200 active; peak bursts up to 4,500 concurrent for ~20 minutes.
- Model: we intend to run a 13B open model q4/8-bit quantized variant for latency-sensitive routes and a 70B quantized variant for high-quality summarization jobs.
- SLA targets: P95 gen latency <= 220ms for short chat paths; background summarization latency okay up to 4s.
- Token burn: ~6M tokens/day average, ~18M tokens/day peak.

Can Redwood run a sizing validation (including KV/prefix cache behavior, burst scaling rehearsals, and a cutover weekend plan with rollback steps)? We also attached our initial SLA requirements spreadsheet.

What's realistic for a sizing run and a dry-run cutover rehearsal? Procurement timeline: we need reserved capacity committed by 2026-09-10 to hit our Q4 deliverables.

Thanks,
Jamie
Jamie Lee

Jamie — thanks, this is perfect context. We can definitely run a focused sizing validation and baking weeks for cutover. Proposed approach (summary):

1) Intake and telemetry pass (3 business days): Redwood ingests a 72-hour traffic dump or synthetic replay (you pick). We collect sequence length distributions, prompt templates, and the KV/prefix hit ratio.
2) Sizing snapshot (2 business days): We run microbenchmarks across both model variants to recommend instance counts, allocation per model, and headroom for burst concurrency.
3) Stressproof rehearsal (2 days): Two rehearsals — one midweek spike test (simulate 4.5k conc for 20m) and one weekend full dry-run cutover to exercise routing, failover and rollback.
4) Cutover weekend and acceptance (Friday rehearsals + Saturday cutover; rollback window on Sunday morning).

Proposed dates to align with your procurement target:
- Intake start: 2026-08-25
- Sizing snapshot complete: 2026-08-30
- Rehearsals: 2026-09-02 and 2026-09-04
- Cutover weekend: 2026-09-11 → 2026-09-12 (aligns to your commit deadline)

Deliverables: sizing spreadsheet, per-route latency profiles, KV cache hit-rate recommendations, quantization profile notes, and a step-by-step cutover/runbook.

Questions for you:
- Would you prefer a synthetic replay (we can generate) or a short 72-hour real traffic export?
- Any blackout windows for rehearsals?

I'll put Ben down as the tech lead for sizing and Karthik for runtime/config tuning. If Procurement wants a mutual action plan, loop Neha and we'll draft.

— Sofia

Quick technical readout from my side — flagged a few constraints and initial sizing assumptions. Attachment: initial-sizing-snapshot.csv (CSV; 18 KB).

Assumptions I used for the snapshot:
- Model latencies (p50/p95) measured on our dedicated X1 instances for 13B q4 and 70B q8 at your average prompt length of 120 tokens and average response 40 tokens.
- Baseline warm KV cache for typical chat prefixes yields a 35–48% token-level cache hit rate; with prefix caching improvements we can push to 55–60% for templated prompts.
- For the concurrency profile: sustain 1.2k conc => ~8 X1 GPUs for 13B path with batching window tuned; burst to 4.5k conc for 20m => autoscale target ~28 X1 GPUs (adds 3–5s scale latency if cold).

Sizing notes / mitigations:
- We recommend reserving 30 GPUs for the 13B path (allowing burst headroom and staging runway) and 8 dedicated GPUs for the 70B summarization pool (background jobs run on separate queues to avoid P95 regression).
- Enable KV prefix caching and an aggressive pre-warm plan for scheduled burst times.
- Quantization: use q4f16 for the 13B chat path to keep latency below 220ms more reliably. 70B can run q8 with more inference parallelism.

Open items for Jamie:
- Do you have recent 72-hour traffic export or want us to synthetic-replay with your templates?
- Any hard guardrails for scale-up >30 GPUs (budget/contract constraints)?

— Ben

- Procurement constraint: we cannot commit to >25 GPUs baseline without signoff — can Redwood demonstrate safe operation with 25 GPUs and graceful degradation strategies above that?

Also, can you outline the acceptance tests you'll run during the cutover weekend? We'll want them in writing for SRE and our on-call.

— Jamie

All — good momentum. Confirming the plan and owners below, plus the cutover weekend runbook outline. Rehearsals and cutover align with your procurement timeline.

Schedule (final):
- 2026-08-25 — intake starts (Jamie sends 72-hour export)
- 2026-08-28 — sizing snapshot delivered (Ben)
- 2026-09-02 — midweek synthetic spike rehearsal (Ben lead)
- 2026-09-04 — weekend full dry-run cutover rehearsal (end-to-end; Sofia lead)
- 2026-09-11 18:00 PDT — cutover kick (Friday rehearsals earlier that day)
- 2026-09-12 02:00 PDT — acceptance window close; Sunday 06:00 PDT rollback window until 08:00 if needed

Runbook highlights:
- Pre-cutover checklist: traffic drain for non-critical jobs, snapshot KV baseline, warm cache pre-population, proxy DNS TTL lowered to 30s.
- Acceptance tests (automated): synthetic p95 latency probes per-route (goal: <=220ms for chat), sampled session continuity (audit IDs compared), KV cache hit-rate >= 45% for templated prompts, and cost burn sanity checks.
- Rollback plan: switch routing back to hosted via weighted routing shift (90/10) then 0 within 90 minutes if regressions observed; session continuity best-effort via sticky session ids and rehydration.

Action items: 
- Jamie: send sanitized 72-hour export by 2026-08-26 EOD (owner: Jamie)
- Ben: deliver sizing spreadsheet and instance counts by 2026-08-28 (owner: Ben)
- Karthik: pre-warm scripts and cache configurations for rehearsal by 2026-09-01 (owner: Karthik)
- Neha: draft MSA addendum and DocuSign envelope targeting signatures before 2026-09-09 (owner: Neha)
- Sofia: coordinate rehearsals, host runbook doc, and finalize acceptance test harness.

If anyone has blackout windows or additional constraints please call them out by EOD Monday. We'll post the runbook to the shared drive and the HubSpot deal record.

Thanks all — looking forward to the rehearsal.
